responses.title: The Button Sorting Switch
story: Imagine the box as a mail sorter. Every time you press a button on the remote, a little note with a code number arrives. The switch statement on line 169 reads that number and decides which slot it belongs in.
Each case is one slot. If the note says up, the box tilts up one step. If it says left, the box turns left a little. The word break means the sorting is done, so the box skips the other slots.
The OK button fires one dart. The star button fires all six darts. Button 1 makes the turret nod yes three times, and button 2 makes it shake no three times.
If you press a button that has no case, like 5, nothing happens. The note has no slot, so the box just waits for the next press.

steps.label: Read the code
steps.detail: The switch looks at the command number the remote just sent.

steps.label: Tilt buttons
steps.detail: Up and down each tilt the barrel one step by calling upMove or downMove.

steps.label: Turn buttons
steps.detail: Left and right spin the turret a short burst with leftMove or rightMove.

steps.label: Fire buttons
steps.detail: OK fires one dart, and star spins the drum to fire all six.

steps.label: Head shakes
steps.detail: Button 1 nods yes and button 2 shakes no, three times each.

steps.label: No match
steps.detail: If the code matches no case, the switch ends and nothing moves.

responses.metaphor: The switch is like a mail sorter who reads each note and drops it into the right slot.
responses.watch_for: Press OK for one dart, then star for all six, and notice that button 5 does nothing because it has no case.
